headline: South Asia: Israeli strike kills 6 at southern Gaza hospital: civil defence
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Israeli strike kills 6 at southern Gaza hospital: civil defence.
- Western Russia: Ukraine War Turns Black Sea Into World’s Deadliest Shipping Lane – WSJ.
- Asia: Cold War lessons for the AI age: how a US-China hotline could help stop a nuclear attack.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Holness eyes foreign labour for NaRRA.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 13 hours ago: Holness eyes foreign labour for NaRRA.
Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness has reiterated that the National Reconstruction and Resilience Authority (NaRRA) may have to source some of the skills needed to rebuild western Jamaica from overseas amid a shortage of skilled labour in the construction industry. Speaking at a National Housing Trust (NHT) ceremony at which 25 young Jamaicans were awarded scholarships under the agency’s Construction Scholarship Programme, Holness said it was time for the industry to expand its capacity to meet the country’s demands.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 13 hours ago: Gov’t slapped with massive payout - Judge awards St Elizabeth woman more than $10 million in damages for negligent medical care.
The Government has been ordered to pay more than J$10 million in damages to a St Elizabeth woman for negligent medical care she received from a doctor at a public clinic, which left her in pain for months. June Hyman was awarded J$7.9 million in general damages, with interest at three per cent from August 2013 to September this year. She was also awarded special damages of US$16,312 (approximately J$2.5 million) and J$271,604, following an assessment of damages hearing in the Supreme Court on October 9.
United States - bottom line: Army formally activates public affairs school.
- Military Times, just now: Army formally activates public affairs school.
The Army formally activated its U.S. Army Public Affairs School, a milestone toward the goal of continuously upgrading strategic military communications.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: 3 Iranian-backed men indicted in attempted plot on RAF Fairford.
Three men, with one working from jail, allegedly conspired to commit around 20 terrorist attacks across the U.S. and Europe, including the plot on RAF Fairford, on behalf of Iran-aligned terrorist networks.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

Whether fretting about the Iran war — or picturing life without him — the U.S. president is looming large in the minds of politicians and campaigners at the global climate summit.

AFRICA

- Africanews, 4 hours ago: Ukraine: Russian drone attack sparks major fire in Kyiv residential building.
A Russian drone strike sparked a major fire at an apartment building in Kyiv, Ukraine, early on Thursday. Residents fled to safety as firefighters battled the flames and rescue workers helped people at the scene.

South Sudan and UN peacekeepers are being accused of failing to act on warnings of a massacre that killed more than 200 people in March.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 14 hours ago: Sudan: OCHA Reports 71 Aid Workers Killed in Sudan in 2025 As Humanitarian Funding Crisis Deepens.
[Dabanga] Amsterdam -- At least 71 humanitarian workers were killed and 28 injured in Sudan during 2025, as attacks on aid operations, restricted access and severe funding shortages undermined the delivery of life-saving assistance, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).
- Africanews, 20 hours ago: Spain: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after peaceful general strike march.
Burning barricades and clashes with riot police erupted in Barcelona after a peaceful march against soaring housing costs. Police used projectiles to disperse masked protesters as violence spread through the city centre.

[DW] Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of allegations that he had used artificial intelligence to write his award-winning short story, The Blue Fighter. The reports had emerged after an article in The Atlantic cited results from an AI detection tool, which suggested that the story may have been generated by artificial intelligence.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 8 hours ago: Mozambique: Valá Calls for Economic Planning Focused On Concrete Results.
[AIM] Maputo -- Mozambican Minister of Planning and Development, Salim Valá, calls for a shift in the approach to economic planning, moving away from a resource-centered economy toward one oriented toward concrete results, capable of generating employment, income, and better living conditions for the population.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Israeli strike kills 6 at southern Gaza hospital: civil defence.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, Africanews, ABC News Australia, just now: Israeli strike kills 6 at southern Gaza hospital: civil defence.
An Israeli strike killed six people and wounded around 20 at Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, a civil defence official told AFP on Thursday. The Israeli military confirmed the strike. Gaza’s civil defence agency said the bodies of those killed and more than 20 people wounded in the strike had been recovered from a building at the medical complex. “The death toll from the Israeli strike inside Nasser Medical Complex, west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, has risen to six,” civil defence spokesperson Mahmoud Bassal told AFP. Nasser Hospital confirmed the six deaths in a statement.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: President, PM condole martyrdom of 10 policemen in Kohat, vow to continue fight against terrorism.
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday expressed grief over the martyrdom of 10 police personnel in a terrorist attack on a police team in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kohat district. Eighteen terrorists were killed and 10 police personnel were martyred on Wednesday when a police team came under attack while returning from an operation against elements involved in illegal gold mining. In his message, the president said the sacrifices of the KP police in the fight against terrorism were a source of pride for the entire nation.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: 3 terrorists killed, 2 civilians dead as attack on Mastung post repulsed: state media.
Security forces killed three terrorists on the N-25 highway in Balochistan’s Mastung district while repulsing an attack on Kandawa Post, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported on Thursday, citing police. According to a spokesperson for Balochistan Police, terrorists belonging to Fitna al Hindustan attempted a “cowardly attack at Kandawa Post on National Highway N-25 using an explosives-laden vehicle”. The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: US marine guard appears to rebuke Hegseth's delegation at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
A US Army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier appeared to rebuke Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s delegation on Wednesday after laughter could be heard as they climbed the steps of the solemn site, according to a video of the incident. Hegseth, his wife and senior aides could be seen taking pictures and speaking to each other on the steps of the memorial at Arlington National Cemetery following a Veterans Day event.

The United States and China should set up a dedicated hotline to help reduce the risk of AI-induced nuclear attacks, analysts have said. The call came amid a fresh push by Washington to prioritise high-level talks on arms controls. In a phone conversation on Wednesday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi agreed that meaningful leader-level conversations would help “advance goals such as peace and denuclearisation”, according to the Department of State. Workers at New Zealand’s largest retailer have had to resort to defecating in the distribution aisles after their bathroom breaks were tracked by artificial intelligence, their union has claimed. More than 300 employees of The Warehouse protested in Auckland and Christchurch on Thursday against technology monitoring them and taking over their jobs, The New Zealand Herald reported. US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu recently faced challenges regarding Iran's nuclear strategy. Trump prefers diplomatic solutions while Netanyahu advocates for military action and regime change in Tehran. Their disagreement highlights political tensions as Netanyahu's leadership faces increasing opposition at home. In Israel, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot is working to form a coalition government.

The Indian Air Force has launched indigenous artificial intelligence applications to improve operational efficiency and safety. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh emphasized the need for greater preparedness against emerging threats during the conference in New Delhi. He highlighted the importance of maintaining the element of surprise and enhancing intelligence mechanisms in military operations. The changing nature of warfare requires focus on drones and advanced weapon systems for future conflicts.

The retrial is necessary after the first trial did not adequately address key pieces of evidence. The court clarified important legal principles related to unrepresented litigants and trial procedures. MTH, the survivor, is once again pursuing damages for the abuse she suffered while in foster care.
